title: Operator triage & runbook: RBAC v2, audit logs, and SAML SSO troubleshooting
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Operator-facing triage guide and reference macros for incidents involving RBAC v2 misconfigurations, missing audit entries, or SAML SSO failures. This doc is intended to be used by SREs, Security on-call, and Support to quickly identify root causes, recover access, and produce consistent customer communications.
runbook:
OVERVIEW:
This runbook covers three common classes of incidents: 1) RBAC v2 role/permission regressions (e.g., users suddenly lose access), 2) missing/partial audit logs (log ingestion/backfill delays), 3) SAML SSO authentication failures (assertion, certificate, metadata issues). Follow the triage checklist below, run the verification commands, and escalate per the escalation policy.

QUICK TRIAGE CHECKLIST (first 10 min):
- Confirm scope: single user / org / all orgs. Gather org-id, user email, timestamp, and operation attempted.
- Check feature flag state: ff status rbac_v2_enabled for org (console or flags dashboard).
- Verify if this is a config change: review last config commit: git log --oneline -- path=infra/iam/roles.yaml -- since="24h"
- Determine if audit logs contain the relevant event (see AUDIT QUERIES). If logs absent, check ingestion pipeline health.

RBAC VERIFICATION COMMANDS:
- CLI: redwoodctl iam roles list --org <ORG_ID>
- Get effective permissions for user: redwoodctl iam simulate --org <ORG_ID> --user <USER_EMAIL> --resource <RESOURCE>
- Validate role bindings: redwoodctl iam bindings get --org <ORG_ID> --role <ROLE_NAME>
- Quick check in Postgres (read-replica): SELECT role_name, member_type, member_id, updated_at FROM iam_role_bindings WHERE org_id = '<ORG_ID>' ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 100;
- If role change is recent, check rollout: gitlab.com/redwood-infra/configs/merge_requests/<MR_ID> and console Rollouts -> RBAC v2 -> <org_id>

AUDIT LOGGING DIAGNOSTICS:
- Primary artifacts: kafka topic audit.events, S3 path s3://redwood-audit/events/YYYY/MM/DD, and BigQuery table `redwood-prod.audit.events`.
- Example BigQuery query (use project redwood-prod):
  SELECT timestamp, org_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, success
  FROM `redwood-prod.audit.events`
  WHERE org_id = '<ORG_ID>' AND timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(TIMESTAMP('<ISO_TS>'), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE) AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(TIMESTAMP('<ISO_TS>'), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE)
  ORDER BY timestamp DESC
- If no rows returned: verify ingestion pipeline:
  - Check Kafka consumer group: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group audit-ingestor
  - Check ingestor pod logs: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/audit-ingestor --tail=200
  - Check S3 writer errors in datadog logs: service:audit-writer AND env:prod AND status:ERROR
- Backfill shortcut: run ad-hoc backfill job (requires approval): kubectl -n infra exec job/audit-backfill -- /app/backfill --org <ORG_ID> --start <ISO_TS> --end <ISO_TS> (note: backfills increment billing; use sparingly)

SAML/SSO TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS:
- Symptoms: login loop, 401/403 on callback, SAML assertion missing attributes.
- Basic checks:
  - Confirm IdP metadata timestamp and metadata.xml in console matches IdP (okta/saml provider)
  - Check TLS cert validity for SAML signing cert; certificate rotation logs: ops/iam/certs/cert-rotation.log
  - Verify clock skew: run time sync check on auth nodes: chronyc tracking
- Example SAML assertion debug (when available from IdP): decode base64 assertion and check for NameID and AttributeStatement. Search for expected attributes: "email", "org_id", "roles".
- Common fixes:
  - If attributes missing: coordinate with customer IdP admin to add attribute mapping (provide sample mapping in SUPPORT MACRO below).
  - If cert expired: rotate signing certificate and trigger metadata refresh (see CERT ROTATION section).

SUPPORT MACROS & MESSAGE TEMPLATES (for L2/Security replies):
- MACRO-SAML-ATTRS-01: "We see the SAML assertion missing the 'org_id' attribute. Please update your IdP mapping to include 'org_id' (SAML attribute name 'urn:redwood:org_id') and retry. See sample mapping: https://confluence.redwood/integrations/saml#sample-attribute-mapping"
- MACRO-RBAC-RESET-02: "We have reset the user's explicit role bindings for <USER_EMAIL> in org <ORG_ID>. Please ask the user to sign out and back in. If they still cannot access X, please provide the timestamp and attempt URL."
- MACRO-AUDIT-MISSING-03: "Our ingestion shows a lag/backfill in audit logs between <start> and <end>. We are running a backfill and will follow up with timeline and affected APIs. Reference: GH PR #4456 and incident runbook."

ESCALATION POLICY:
- If P0 or customer impact is high and not resolvable within 30 minutes: page Security on-call and SRE on-call. Use PagerDuty escalation policy 'SECURITY-ONCALL'.
- Include these artifacts in the incident: org-id, user email, relevant log snippets, last successful role-change MR, and audit query results.
- Postmortem owner: assignee of this ticket unless reassigned.

RECOVERY / MITIGATION SCRIPTS (only ops can run):
- Temporary grant: redwoodctl iam bindings create --org <ORG_ID> --role "org_admin_temp" --member user:<USER_EMAIL> --expires-in 1h --reason "Emergency access for triage"
- Revoke temp grant: redwoodctl iam bindings delete --org <ORG_ID> --role "org_admin_temp" --member user:<USER_EMAIL>

CERT ROTATION (SAML signing cert) - QUICK STEPS:
1) Upload new cert to secrets manager: aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id prod/saml/cert --secret-binary fileb://new-cert.pem
2) Trigger metadata refresh: POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/admin/saml/refresh?org=<ORG_ID> (internal endpoint)
3) Validate login with test account and confirm new certificate fingerprints in metadata.

NOTES ON PRIVACY & AUDIT TRAIL:
- When handling customer-provided SAML assertions or logs, redact PII before pasting into Slack. Use [REDACT] for user emails.
